documents.title: Corporate Credit Risk Appetite and Single-Name Limit Framework
documents.regulatory_anchor: OSFI Guideline B-3 (Sound Reproducible Underwriting), OSFI E-21 (Operational Risk and Resilience)
documents.content:
PURPOSE. Establishes the credit risk appetite for corporate and institutional clients of the Capital Markets segment and the single-name limit framework that expresses it.

SINGLE-NAME LIMIT DEFINITION. The single-name limit is the maximum aggregate credit exposure the firm will carry to one obligor group, measured as the sum of (a) funded loans drawn, (b) contingent exposure including letters of credit and undrawn committed facilities weighted at the applicable credit conversion factor, (c) derivative mark-to-market plus potential future exposure, and (d) settlement and daylight exposure. Undrawn uncommitted lines are excluded from utilisation but are disclosed in every limit report.

LIMIT SETTING BY INTERNAL RISK RATING. Limits are set as a function of the internal risk rating (IG-1 strongest to IG-12 weakest) and the tenor of the exposure.

| Internal rating | Indicative single-name ceiling | Maximum final maturity |
| IG-1 to IG-4 | CAD 900m | 10 years |
| IG-5 to IG-6 | CAD 500m | 7 years |
| IG-7 to IG-8 | CAD 350m | 5 years |
| IG-9 to IG-10 | CAD 200m | 3 years |
| IG-11 and below | no new exposure; run-off only | n/a |

UTILISATION TRIGGERS. Utilisation of a single-name limit is reported at each month end and monitored continuously.
- Green: below 85 per cent of limit. Normal course.
- Amber: 85 to 99 per cent. New exposure requires the Credit Risk limit owner's written concurrence before commitment. A utilisation forecast for the next two quarters must accompany any request.
- Breach: 100 per cent or above. Immediate escalation to the Credit Committee, no new exposure of any tenor, and a remediation plan within five business days.

HEADROOM IS NOT AUTHORITY. Available headroom under a single-name limit does not by itself authorise a new commitment. Every incremental commitment must independently satisfy the sector concentration limits under CP-002, the underwriting commitment authority under CP-003, and the covenant pro-forma test under CP-005 where the obligor is subject to financial covenants.

ANNUAL REVIEW. Every obligor with an active limit is subject to a full credit review at least annually. A limit whose review date has passed is deemed frozen at current utilisation until the review is completed; no increase may be approved against a stale review.

RELATIONSHIP PRESSURE. Coverage may not present an indicative hold size to a client before the limit position has been confirmed with the named limit owner. An indication given and then withdrawn is a client-facing conduct issue as well as a credit issue.

documents.title: Sector and Portfolio Concentration Limit Policy
documents.regulatory_anchor: OSFI Guideline B-3; internal ICAAP concentration appetite
documents.content:
PURPOSE. Constrains aggregate exposure by sector, sub-sector and correlated risk factor so that no single macro driver can impair a disproportionate share of the corporate portfolio.

SECTOR CEILINGS (FY26). Energy CAD 3,200m. Materials CAD 2,100m. Industrials CAD 2,400m. Real Estate CAD 1,800m. Utilities CAD 2,600m. Ceilings are reset annually with the risk appetite statement and may be varied intra-year only by the Chief Risk Officer with Board Risk Committee notification.

ENERGY SUB-SECTOR SUB-CEILINGS. Within the Energy ceiling: Midstream and Infrastructure CAD 1,600m; Exploration and Production CAD 900m; Energy Services CAD 400m; Energy Distribution CAD 500m. Sub-ceilings are hard - unused headroom in one sub-sector does not create capacity in another.

SECTOR UTILISATION TRIGGERS. The same green / amber / breach convention as CP-001 applies at the sector level.
- At or above 85 per cent of a sector ceiling, the sector is AMBER. Every new commitment in that sector, regardless of the obligor's own single-name headroom, requires Portfolio Management sign-off in addition to the normal credit approval, and must be accompanied by an identified offset - a syndication, a sell-down, a maturing facility or an approved distribution plan.
- At 100 per cent, the sector is closed to new commitments.

ORIGINATE-TO-DISTRIBUTE EXPECTATION. Where a sector is amber, the default expectation for new lead-arranged transactions is that the firm's final hold is materially below its arrangement position, with the distribution plan documented before commitment rather than after. A commitment made on the assumption that distribution will succeed, without a documented plan, is a control weakness.

CORRELATION OVERLAY. Midstream obligors whose cash flows depend on the same basin, the same egress corridor or the same counterparty offtake are treated as correlated for stress purposes and are reported as a correlated cluster even where they sit within separate sub-ceilings.

DISCLOSURE IN PITCH MATERIALS. Sector capacity constraints are internal. They may not be disclosed to a client, a competitor or a syndicate participant, and may not be used as a negotiating position with a client. Where capacity constrains the firm's response to a client request, coverage states only that the hold size is subject to internal approval.

documents.title: Underwriting Commitment Authority and DCM New-Issue Approval
documents.regulatory_anchor: NI 51-102 continuous disclosure; CIRO underwriting conduct rules; OSFI B-3
documents.content:
PURPOSE. Sets the authority required to commit the firm's balance sheet to an underwriting, a bought deal, a bridge or a lead-arranged loan commitment.

APPROVAL MATRIX - LOAN COMMITMENTS (final hold sought).
| Commitment sought | Approver | Standard turnaround |
| up to CAD 75m | Director, Credit Risk (sector) | 2 business days |
| CAD 76m to CAD 150m | Credit Committee (written resolution permitted) | 3 business days |
| CAD 151m to CAD 250m | Credit Committee (convened) | 5 business days |
| above CAD 250m | Credit Committee plus Chief Risk Officer | 5 business days, no expedited path |
| any amount where the sector is AMBER under CP-002 | the above, plus Portfolio Management sign-off and a documented distribution plan | unchanged |
| any amount where the obligor's single-name limit is AMBER under CP-001 | the above, plus the named limit owner's written concurrence | unchanged |

APPROVAL MATRIX - SECURITIES UNDERWRITING.
| Underwriting position | Approver |
| up to CAD 150m | Head of DCM plus Director, Credit Risk |
| CAD 151m to CAD 400m | Underwriting Committee |
| above CAD 400m, or any equity bought deal | Underwriting Committee plus Chief Risk Officer |

UNDERWRITING COMMITMENT LIMIT. Each obligor carries a separate underwriting commitment limit that is distinct from, and does not consume, the single-name credit limit until the commitment is drawn or the securities are retained. Utilisation of an underwriting commitment limit at zero does not imply that a commitment is pre-approved.

AMEND-AND-EXTEND AND UPSIZE TRANSACTIONS. An increase in a committed facility - whether framed as an upsize, an accordion exercise or a new tranche - is a new commitment for the purposes of this policy and is approved on the incremental amount at the authority level for the resulting total hold, not the increment alone. An extension of maturity beyond the tenor ceiling in CP-001 for the obligor's rating requires Credit Committee approval irrespective of size.

INDICATIONS TO CLIENTS. No hold size, no price talk and no structure may be indicated to a client as a firm commitment before the approval above is obtained. Coverage may discuss indicative market terms provided the indication is expressly stated to be subject to internal approval and the qualification is recorded in the call report under CP-014.

CONFLICT WITH RESEARCH. Where the firm holds an underwriting mandate or is in active pursuit of one, Research's independence obligations under CP-008 apply. The existence of a pitch does not restrict Research; being wall-crossed does.

documents.title: Counterparty Credit Risk, CSA Terms and Margin Policy for Corporate Derivatives
documents.regulatory_anchor: OSFI Guideline B-7 (Derivatives Sound Practices); uncleared margin requirements
documents.content:
PURPOSE. Governs the credit terms on which derivative business is transacted with corporate clients, including the pre-settlement exposure line, collateral arrangements and the treatment of unmargined corporate hedging.

PRE-SETTLEMENT EXPOSURE (PSE) LINE. Every corporate derivative counterparty requires an approved PSE line, sized on a potential future exposure basis at the 95th percentile over the life of the trade. The PSE line is a sub-limit of the obligor's single-name credit limit under CP-001 and consumes it - derivative capacity is not additive to lending capacity.

PSE UTILISATION TRIGGER. A PSE line moves to AMBER at 75 per cent utilisation, not at the 85 per cent used for funded limits under CP-001. The tighter trigger exists because potential future exposure is a model output rather than a measured balance: it moves with volatility and with the passage of time even when no new trade is done, so a line that looks comfortable at month end can be tight by the next repricing. From 75 per cent, any new structure requires the PSE line owner's written concurrence before solicitation, and the request must state whether the headroom consumed is expected to amortise or to grow over the life of the trade.

UNMARGINED CORPORATE HEDGING. Corporate clients hedging genuine commercial exposure may transact unmargined where the internal risk rating is IG-8 or better and the PSE line is approved. Below IG-8, a Credit Support Annex with a zero threshold is required. Unmargined status is reviewed at every annual credit review and on any downgrade.

TENOR. Unmargined derivative tenor is capped at the obligor's maximum final maturity under CP-001 and, separately, at 5 years for commodity derivatives regardless of rating, because commodity potential future exposure is materially more volatile than rates or FX at equivalent tenor.

COMMODITY-SPECIFIC ADD-ON. Commodity derivative PSE is calculated with a sector add-on. Differential and basis trades - where the exposure is the spread between two benchmarks rather than an outright price - carry a higher add-on than outright trades of the same notional because the historical spread distribution is fatter-tailed. Sales may not quote a differential structure on the basis of the outright add-on.

WRONG-WAY RISK. A hedge whose mark-to-market moves in the firm's favour precisely when the client's ability to pay deteriorates is specific wrong-way risk and requires explicit Credit Risk identification and pricing. Producer hedges in the energy sector are a standing wrong-way risk category: a producer hedging downside price risk owes the bank when prices rise, which is generally when the producer is strongest - this is favourable-way and acceptable. The reverse structure, where the client is short the commodity, must be flagged.

PRE-CLEARANCE BEFORE SOLICITATION. Corporate Sales must confirm available PSE line headroom with Credit Risk before soliciting a new structure that would materially increase notional. Pricing a structure the credit line cannot support is a client-facing failure and is reportable.

CROSS-DEFAULT AND CLOSE-OUT. All corporate derivative documentation must include cross-default to the obligor's principal credit facility. Where the firm is both a lender and a derivative counterparty, the close-out and enforcement sequencing must be agreed with the Loan Syndications desk before a default event, not during one.

documents.title: Financial Covenant Monitoring and Pro-Forma Testing Standard
documents.owner: Head of Portfolio Management, Corporate Credit
documents.regulatory_anchor: OSFI Guideline B-3; internal credit administration standard
documents.content:
PURPOSE. Sets the standard for monitoring financial covenants and for testing the effect of a proposed new transaction on covenant headroom before the transaction is offered to the client.

MONITORING CADENCE. Covenants are tested on receipt of the borrower's compliance certificate, at the frequency specified in the credit agreement, and independently recalculated by Credit Risk from the borrower's filed financial statements. A covenant calculation accepted from the borrower without independent recalculation is not a completed test.

HEADROOM BANDS. Headroom is expressed in the covenant's own unit - turns for leverage and coverage ratios, currency for net worth tests, percentage for basket tests.
- Comfortable: more than 0.75 turns, or more than 25 per cent of the threshold.
- Monitor: 0.35 to 0.75 turns, or 10 to 25 per cent. Quarterly commentary required in the portfolio report.
- Tight: below 0.35 turns, or below 10 per cent. Monthly monitoring, a forward-looking four-quarter projection, and notification to the relationship owner. The obligor is not automatically watchlisted, but the rationale for not watchlisting must be recorded.
- Breach: headroom at or below zero. Immediate escalation under CP-001.

MANDATORY PRO-FORMA TEST. Before any of the following is presented to a client, Credit Risk must produce a pro-forma covenant calculation showing the position at the next two scheduled test dates assuming the transaction completes and is fully drawn: (a) an increase in committed debt, including an upsize or accordion; (b) an extension of maturity that changes the amortisation profile; (c) a distribution, buyback or acquisition that the firm is financing; (d) any new derivative whose mark-to-market is included in the covenant definition of debt.

FULLY-DRAWN ASSUMPTION. The pro-forma test assumes the facility is fully drawn at the test date unless the credit agreement expressly excludes undrawn commitments from the debt definition. A pro-forma test run on expected utilisation rather than full availability is not compliant with this standard.

TIMING RELATIVE TO REPORTING. Where a proposed transaction would complete within two quarters of a scheduled test date, the pro-forma test must be completed and signed off by Credit Risk before the pitch is delivered, not before the mandate is signed. Presenting a structure and subsequently discovering that it compresses covenant headroom below the Tight band is a client-facing failure.

EQUITY CURE AND ADD-BACK DISCIPLINE. EBITDA add-backs permitted by the credit agreement - synergies, one-time items, run-rate adjustments from an acquisition - are accepted in the covenant calculation only to the extent the agreement permits, and are separately disclosed in the portfolio report alongside the unadjusted ratio. Where the adjusted and unadjusted ratios straddle a headroom band, the unadjusted ratio governs the internal monitoring band.

RESPONSIBILITY. The pro-forma test is owned by the sector Credit Risk director. Coverage may request it; coverage may not perform it, waive it, or present the transaction while it is outstanding.

documents.title: KYC and AML Periodic Refresh Standard for Corporate and Institutional Clients
documents.regulatory_anchor: PCMLTFA and FINTRAC requirements; OSFI Guideline B-8
documents.content:
PURPOSE. Sets the periodic refresh cycle for corporate and institutional client due diligence and the consequences of an overdue refresh.

REFRESH CYCLE BY RISK RATING. Low risk: 36 months. Medium risk: 24 months. High risk: 12 months. Politically exposed person connections, high-risk jurisdictions and complex ownership structures move a client to high risk irrespective of size or tenure.

TRIGGERS FOR OUT-OF-CYCLE REFRESH. A change of control; a material change in beneficial ownership above 25 per cent; a change in the jurisdiction of incorporation or principal operations; adverse media of a financial-crime nature; a new product that changes the client's risk profile, including first-time use of cross-border cash management or physical commodity settlement.

CONSEQUENCES OF AN OVERDUE REFRESH. A refresh that has passed its due date does not automatically suspend the relationship, but from the due date the following apply without exception.
- No new products may be opened.
- No increase to any committed facility may be completed.
- No new derivative relationship documentation may be executed.
- Existing facilities and existing derivative positions continue to be serviced.

GRACE PERIOD. There is no grace period. A refresh 'in progress' at the due date is an overdue refresh.

SEQUENCING WITH CREDIT APPROVAL. Credit approval may be sought and granted while a refresh is outstanding, but the facility may not be documented, executed or funded until the refresh completes. Coverage is responsible for surfacing the refresh date at the point a transaction is contemplated, not at the point of documentation - a transaction that clears credit and then stalls on KYC is an avoidable client-facing failure and is reported as such.

CLIENT COMMUNICATION. Requests for refresh documentation are made by Client Onboarding, copying the relationship owner. Coverage may follow up but may not accept documentation directly or represent to a client that a refresh is complete.

RECORD. The refresh due date, current status and days to due are surfaced on the client record and are reported in every pre-meeting client brief.

documents.title: Sanctions and Restricted-Party Screening Standard
documents.regulatory_anchor: SEMA and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Canada); OFAC; UK OFSI; EU consolidated list
documents.content:
PURPOSE. Sets the screening obligations that apply before the firm transacts with, or on behalf of, any client, counterparty, guarantor, beneficial owner or payment intermediary.

SCREENING POINTS. Screening is performed at onboarding, at every periodic refresh under CP-006, on any change of beneficial ownership, before the execution of any cross-border payment, before the addition of any new guarantor or obligor to a facility, and continuously against list updates.

SCOPE OF SCREENING. The client entity, its parent and controlling entities, beneficial owners at or above 25 per cent, directors and senior officers, and - for physical commodity and trade finance transactions - the counterparties, vessels, ports and jurisdictions in the underlying flow.

OWNERSHIP AGGREGATION. Ownership by listed persons is aggregated. Two listed persons each holding 30 per cent of an entity render that entity restricted even though neither holds a majority. Coverage may not rely on a single-holder test.

POSITIVE OR POSSIBLE MATCH. Any positive or possible match stops the transaction. The matter is referred to Sanctions Compliance and may not be progressed, discussed with the client, or dispositioned by the business under any circumstance. Tipping off is prohibited.

SECTOR-SPECIFIC EXPOSURE. Energy sector clients carry elevated screening relevance because physical flows, offtake counterparties, marine transport and terminal counterparties can introduce sanctioned nexus that the corporate obligor itself does not carry. A clean screen on the obligor is not a clean screen on the transaction.

MEETING PREPARATION. A pre-meeting client brief must state the date and outcome of the most recent screen. A brief that omits the screening status is incomplete. Where a screen is outstanding, the brief must say so rather than omit the field.

documents.title: Information Barriers, Wall-Crossing and the Restricted List Procedure
documents.regulatory_anchor: NI 31-103 conflicts provisions; CIRO Rule 3800 series (research restrictions); provincial securities legislation on insider trading and tipping
documents.content:
PURPOSE. Governs the separation between the private side of the firm, which receives material non-public information in the course of mandated or contemplated transactions, and the public side, which trades, publishes research and covers clients on public information only.

SIDES OF THE WALL. Private side: Investment Banking, Loan Syndications where non-public transaction information is held, and any individual specifically wall-crossed. Public side: Research, Sales and Trading, and coverage staff who have not been wall-crossed. Credit Risk sits above the wall for its own purposes and is wall-crossed transaction by transaction.

WALL-CROSSING. Wall-crossing is performed only by the Control Room, only with a recorded business justification, and only for named individuals. Being on the coverage team does not confer crossed status. A crossed individual is added to the crossing log with the date, the transaction reference and the expected expiry.

OBLIGATIONS OF A CROSSED INDIVIDUAL. A crossed individual must not disclose the information to any person not on the crossing log, including their own coverage colleagues and their own manager unless that manager is separately crossed. They must not trade the security, must not recommend it, and must not use the information in any client conversation. They may continue their normal duties on the name using public information only, but where the distinction cannot be reliably maintained, they must recuse.

OBLIGATIONS OF THE PUBLIC SIDE. Public-side staff must not be told that a crossing exists, must not be told who is crossed, and must not infer or ask. A public-side employee who becomes aware that a crossing exists must report it to the Control Room immediately.

RESTRICTED LIST EFFECTS. When a name is placed on the restricted list, the following apply for the duration of the restriction: Research may not initiate, publish, update, change a rating or change a target price on the name, and may not participate in marketing for the name; Sales and Trading may not solicit business in the name, though unsolicited client orders may be executed on a strictly agency basis with Control Room notification; principal risk-taking in the name is suspended; and no new derivative structure connected to the restricted subject matter may be solicited.

WHAT REMAINS PERMITTED. Coverage of the client continues. Existing facilities continue to be administered. A pitch based exclusively on public information may proceed provided no crossed individual contributes non-public content to it and the pitch does not concern the restricted subject matter. Where there is any doubt whether a proposed pitch touches the restricted subject matter, the doubt is resolved by the Control Room, not by the business.

ESCALATION, NOT SILENT RESOLUTION. Where a commercial objective and a restriction appear to conflict, the conflict is escalated to the Control Room and stated plainly. It is not resolved by narrowing the description of the pitch, by substituting an uncrossed presenter, or by proceeding on the view that the restriction was probably not intended to cover the situation.

EXPIRY. Restrictions expire only when the Control Room removes them. A stated expected expiry date is an expectation, not an authorisation to resume on that date.

documents.title: Material Non-Public Information - Identification, Handling and Personal Trading
documents.regulatory_anchor: Provincial securities legislation - insider trading and tipping prohibitions; NI 51-102
documents.content:
PURPOSE. Defines material non-public information, sets the handling standard, and states the personal trading consequences.

DEFINITION. Information is material if a reasonable investor would consider it important in making an investment decision, or if it would reasonably be expected to have a significant effect on the market price or value of a security. It is non-public until it has been generally disclosed and the market has had a reasonable opportunity to absorb it.

ILLUSTRATIVE CATEGORIES IN CORPORATE BANKING. A contemplated acquisition, disposal or merger. A contemplated equity or debt issuance not yet announced. A change in dividend policy. A covenant waiver request or an anticipated breach. A material change in a borrowing base. A significant asset impairment. A change of chief executive or chief financial officer. Knowledge that a client has approached the firm about any of the foregoing is itself material non-public information, even where no mandate exists and the approach may not proceed.

BORROWER INFORMATION FROM THE LENDING RELATIONSHIP. Information received in a lending capacity - compliance certificates, management forecasts, borrowing base reports, waiver requests - is confidential client information and, where material, is also non-public information. It may not be shared with the public side, may not inform Research, and may not inform trading. Aggregation of individually immaterial lending information into a material picture is subject to the same restriction.

GENERAL DISCLOSURE IS NOT INFERENCE. A public announcement makes the announced facts public. It does not make public any additional non-public detail the firm holds about the same subject. Where a transaction is publicly announced, the firm's non-public knowledge of the pipeline, the timetable or the alternatives considered remains restricted.

PERSONAL TRADING. Personal trading in a security while in possession of material non-public information about it is prohibited without exception. Pre-clearance is required for all employee trades in single names covered by the firm. Restricted list names are blocked at the pre-clearance system level.

REPORTING. Any employee who believes they have received material non-public information, whether or not they sought it, must contact the Control Room the same business day. Uncertainty about materiality is resolved by reporting, not by judgement.

documents.title: Product Suitability and Derivatives Appropriateness for Corporate Clients
documents.regulatory_anchor: NI 31-103 know-your-product and suitability; CIRO business conduct rules
documents.content:
PURPOSE. Sets the appropriateness standard for offering derivative and structured products to corporate clients.

HEDGE VERSUS SPECULATION. Derivative business with a corporate client is offered on the basis that it hedges an identified commercial exposure. The exposure being hedged must be documented before the structure is proposed - the underlying volume, the tenor, the benchmark and the direction of the client's natural position.

HEDGE RATIO DISCIPLINE. A proposed structure whose notional exceeds the documented underlying exposure over the same tenor is not a hedge. Notional above 100 per cent of documented exposure requires written justification and Global Markets Compliance sign-off, and may not be presented as risk reduction.

COMPLEXITY TIERING. Tier 1 - vanilla forwards, swaps and purchased options: standard process. Tier 2 - collars, participating forwards, basis and differential swaps: a written payoff illustration under at least three scenarios including the adverse case, delivered before execution. Tier 3 - leveraged, knock-in or knock-out, or path-dependent structures: Tier 2 requirements plus the client's written acknowledgement of the leverage or barrier feature, and approval by the Head of Corporate Sales.

DIFFERENTIAL AND BASIS STRUCTURES. Differential structures are Tier 2 at minimum because the client is exposed to the relationship between two benchmarks rather than to an outright price. The scenario illustration must include a scenario in which the differential moves against the client while the outright price moves in the client's favour, because that is the case clients most frequently do not anticipate.

CLIENT SOPHISTICATION IS NOT A WAIVER. Corporate treasury sophistication may shorten the explanation. It does not remove the requirement to document the underlying exposure, to deliver the scenario illustration, or to obtain the acknowledgement where the tier requires one.

CREDIT PRE-CLEARANCE. No structure may be solicited before the pre-settlement exposure line headroom is confirmed under CP-004.

RECORD. The documented exposure, the scenario illustration, the tier, the approvals and the client acknowledgement form the suitability file and are retained under CP-014.

documents.title: Sustainable Finance Framework and Sustainability-Linked Structure Eligibility
documents.regulatory_anchor: OSFI Guideline B-15 (Climate Risk Management); CSA climate-related disclosure expectations; ICMA and LMA principles
documents.content:
PURPOSE. Sets the eligibility and review standard for sustainability-linked loans, sustainability-linked bonds, green and transition instruments arranged by the firm.

STRUCTURE TYPES. Use-of-proceeds instruments (green, transition) require an eligible project category and proceeds tracking. Sustainability-linked instruments (SLL, SLB) require key performance indicators and sustainability performance targets with a pricing adjustment on achievement or failure.

KPI QUALITY STANDARD. A key performance indicator must be material to the issuer's core business, measurable on a consistent and disclosed methodology, externally verifiable by an independent assurance provider, and benchmarked against the issuer's own historical performance and its peers. Intensity metrics are acceptable where absolute metrics are distorted by acquisitions or disposals, but the framework must state which is used and why.

AMBITION TEST. A sustainability performance target must represent an improvement beyond a business-as-usual trajectory. A target the issuer would meet without additional action does not qualify. Where an issuer has recently completed an acquisition that mechanically changes an intensity metric, the baseline must be restated so the target is not met through portfolio composition alone.

PRICING ADJUSTMENT. The step-up and step-down must be symmetrical and economically meaningful relative to the instrument's margin. A one basis point adjustment on a facility priced in the low hundreds is not meaningful and will not be approved.

SECOND-PARTY OPINION. A second-party opinion is required for any public sustainability-linked or use-of-proceeds instrument before launch, and for a private sustainability-linked loan above CAD 250m.

GREENWASHING CONTROL. Marketing material may not describe an instrument as sustainable, green or transition-aligned before the framework and the second-party opinion are in place. Indicative discussion with a client is permitted; labelled marketing is not. Every sustainability claim in a pitch book requires an identified evidentiary source and Sustainable Finance review, and the review must be recorded.

SECTOR CONTEXT. For energy and midstream issuers, transition-linked structures are in scope where the KPIs address the issuer's own operational emissions, methane intensity, water and land reclamation, or safety performance. Downstream combustion emissions outside the issuer's operational control are not an appropriate KPI for a transition-linked instrument arranged under this framework.

documents.title: Gibson Energy Inc. (TSX:GEI) - FY26 Account Plan and Pitch Book Extract
documents.regulatory_anchor: Internal account planning standard; subject to CP-008 and CP-014
documents.content:
SYNTHETIC ACCOUNT PLAN. Every internal figure below is invented for a demonstration. Gibson Energy Inc. is a real public company; nothing here reflects any real bank's actual relationship with it.

RELATIONSHIP SUMMARY. Client since 2011. Coverage tier 1. Internal risk rating IG-6, trend improving, not watchlisted. Public ratings S&P BBB- (stable) / DBRS BBB (low) (stable). Relationship owner: Managing Director, Corporate Coverage - Energy. Coverage banker: Director, Corporate Banking and DCM Origination.

FY26 POSITION AS AT 10 AUGUST 2026. Total committed CAD 465m across five facilities. Total drawn CAD 288.4m. Total measured exposure CAD 341.7m against a single-name limit of CAD 500m, a utilisation of 68.3 per cent - GREEN under CP-001. FY26 year-to-date revenue CAD 8.42m against CAD 7.14m in the same period of FY25, up 17.9 per cent. Estimated wallet share 21.4 per cent, up from 18.9 per cent, ranking second from third.

WHAT DROVE FY26. The July 2026 senior unsecured note offering, on which the firm acted as an active bookrunner, is the single largest revenue contributor at CAD 2.68m of DCM fees year to date. The Chauvin bridge take-out term loan added CAD 1.02m. Commodity derivatives contributed CAD 1.01m and are the one product where the firm holds the number one wallet position.

WHERE THE FIRM IS WEAK. Equity capital markets: zero revenue against an estimated street wallet of CAD 2.8m - the firm has never been on an equity mandate for this client. Trade finance: zero. M&A: CAD 0.45m against an estimated CAD 4.5m street wallet, and the firm was not on the buy-side of the most recent transaction in an advisory capacity beyond a financing role. Cash management is under-penetrated relative to the lending position.

FY26 H2 OBJECTIVES. (1) Revolver upsize and one-year extension - move the syndicate facility from CAD 1.10bn to CAD 1.35bn with the firm's hold moving from CAD 165m to CAD 210m, as Co-Lead Arranger and Joint Bookrunner; indicative fees CAD 1.85m. (2) Commodity and FX hedging overlay for the Chauvin volumes - approximately CAD 240m notional over 24 months across a WTI-WCS differential structure and a CAD/USD forward strip; indicative revenue CAD 0.94m. (3) Position for the 2027 maturity refinancing, indicatively CAD 350m, seeking joint bookrunner economics; indicative fees CAD 1.12m.

KNOWN CONSTRAINTS THE TEAM MUST CARRY INTO ANY PITCH. The Energy sector concentration limit is AMBER at 85.8 per cent under CP-002, so the incremental hold requires Portfolio Management sign-off and a documented distribution plan. The proposed total hold of CAD 210m falls in the CAD 151m to CAD 250m band under CP-003 and therefore requires a convened Credit Committee. Leverage covenant headroom is 0.32 turns, inside the Tight band under CP-005, so a pro-forma test is mandatory before the pitch is delivered. The KYC periodic refresh is due 30 September 2026 and, under CP-006, no committed facility increase may be executed after that date until the refresh completes.

CLIENT PRIORITIES AS UNDERSTOOD. Cost of capital and covenant flexibility following the acquisition. Maintaining the investment grade rating. Reducing exposure to the WTI-WCS differential. Interest in a transition-linked structure but no framework in place.

COMPETITIVE PICTURE. The firm is second in wallet. Competitor A leads the lending relationship and the letter of credit business. Competitor C leads DCM by fee volume. Competitor B is making a concerted approach on rates and FX. The firm's defensible position is commodity derivatives, where it is first.

DO NOT DISCLOSE. Internal risk rating, single-name limit, sector capacity position, wallet share estimates and competitor rankings are internal. None may be shown to the client or referenced in a client-facing document.

documents.title: Midstream and Energy Infrastructure Sector Risk Memo - FY26 Second Half
documents.owner: Director, Credit Risk - Energy and Midstream
documents.regulatory_anchor: Internal sector review standard; OSFI B-15 climate risk considerations
documents.content:
SYNTHETIC SECTOR MEMO. Views and figures below are invented for a demonstration and are not any institution's actual credit view.

SECTOR STANCE. Constructive on contracted midstream infrastructure; cautious on marketing and commodity-margin-dependent earnings; negative on uncontracted gathering exposed to single-basin producer concentration.

WHY THE DISTINCTION MATTERS. Midstream credit quality is a function of contract structure, not of the commodity price. Take-or-pay and cost-of-service contracts with investment grade counterparties produce debt capacity. Percentage-of-proceeds and marketing margin do not, and should be haircut in the internal cash flow view even where the reported EBITDA includes them at full value.

LEVERAGE THROUGH THE ACQUISITION CYCLE. The sector has funded a wave of infrastructure acquisitions with a mix of senior unsecured issuance and revolver drawings. The characteristic pattern is: announce, bridge, term out, deleverage over six to eight quarters. The credit risk sits in the middle of that sequence, where reported leverage is at its peak, the synergies are pro-forma rather than realised, and the covenant headroom is at its thinnest. Obligors in the middle of that sequence warrant the Tight-band monitoring under CP-005 even where the headline rating is unchanged.

ADD-BACK SCRUTINY. Acquisition-related EBITDA add-backs are the most common source of divergence between the borrower's covenant calculation and the independent recalculation. Run-rate synergy add-backs should be tested against realised synergies at each quarter, and the unadjusted ratio should be tracked in parallel.

DIFFERENTIAL RISK. Western Canadian producers and the midstream operators serving them carry exposure to the heavy-light differential, which is driven by egress capacity, refinery turnaround schedules and inventory positioning rather than by the outright crude price. Differential volatility is materially higher than outright volatility at equivalent tenor. This has two consequences: it makes differential hedging genuinely valuable to the client, and it makes differential derivative exposure more expensive in potential future exposure terms under CP-004.

CONCENTRATION AND CORRELATION. The sector concentration position is AMBER. Beyond the aggregate number, the correlated cluster of obligors dependent on the same egress corridor is the relevant exposure for stress purposes. New lead-arranged commitments in the sub-sector should be underwritten with a documented distribution plan rather than an intention to hold.

CLIMATE AND TRANSITION. Under OSFI B-15 the sector's physical and transition risk assessment is refreshed annually. Operational emissions, methane intensity and reclamation obligations are the credit-relevant transition factors for midstream, because they translate into capital expenditure and regulatory cost. Downstream combustion emissions are not a credit driver at the obligor level and should not be presented as one.

WATCH ITEMS FOR H2 FY26. Producer counterparty concentration in gathering contracts. Realisation of acquisition synergies against the pro-forma case. Rate-agency commentary on acquisition-funded leverage. Renewal terms on contracts maturing within 24 months.

documents.title: Client Meeting Conduct, Disclosure and Record-Keeping Standard
documents.owner: Head of Capital Markets Business Conduct
documents.regulatory_anchor: CIRO business conduct rules; NI 31-103 record-keeping; internal books and records standard
documents.content:
PURPOSE. Sets what must be done before, during and after a client meeting, and what may and may not be said.

BEFORE THE MEETING - THE PRE-MEETING BRIEF. A pre-meeting brief is required for any meeting with a corporate or institutional client at chief financial officer level or above. It must state, at minimum: current exposure against limit and the utilisation band; internal risk rating and trend; covenant status including the tightest covenant and its headroom band; KYC refresh status and due date; sanctions screening date and outcome; any restricted list or wall-crossing status affecting attendees or subject matter; open commitments made at the previous meeting and their status; and the specific approvals required for anything the team intends to discuss.

COMPLETENESS. A brief that omits a required field is incomplete. Where a field cannot be populated, the brief states that it could not be populated and why. Omission is not an acceptable substitute for a negative answer.

ATTENDEE CLEARANCE. Where any proposed attendee is on the crossing log for the client, the attendee list and the agenda must be cleared by the Control Room under CP-008 before the meeting. Clearance is sought on the agenda as it stands, not on a narrowed description of it.

DURING THE MEETING - WHAT MAY NOT BE SAID. Internal risk ratings, internal limits, limit utilisation, sector capacity, wallet share estimates, competitor rankings and internal credit views may not be disclosed to the client. Indicative terms may be discussed only where expressly qualified as subject to internal approval. No commitment, hold size or price may be represented as firm before the approval required under CP-003 is in place.

AFTER THE MEETING - THE CALL REPORT. A call report is filed within two business days. It records attendees on both sides, the matters discussed, every indication given and the qualification attached to it, every commitment made by the firm with a named owner and a date, every item of client information received and whether any of it is potentially material non-public information, and the agreed next steps.

MATERIAL NON-PUBLIC INFORMATION RECEIVED IN A MEETING. Where a client discloses something that may be material and non-public, the call report records that it was received and the Control Room is notified the same business day under CP-009. The substance is not circulated in the call report distribution.

COMMITMENT TRACKING. A commitment recorded in a call report is tracked to completion. Open commitments from the previous meeting are a mandatory field in the next pre-meeting brief. Repeatedly carrying forward an unclosed commitment is a relationship management failure and is reported in the quarterly conduct review.

RETENTION. Pre-meeting briefs, call reports, pitch materials in the form delivered, suitability files and Control Room clearances are retained for seven years and are producible on request.
